messages:
Jordan (support): FYI customer (Metricly) opened an escalation — their trace view is dropping spans and some request IDs aren't linking to any trace. They see gaps starting ~2026-03-10 14:00 UTC. Repro steps and IDs below.

Rae (customer-success): Customer reports dashboard charts show traces for ~60% of requests, but their service logs show 100% processed. They want root cause and ETA.

Jordan (support): Repro steps from customer: 1) Send requests with header `X-Req-Id` set to a UUID. 2) Wait 2-5s then query /traces?request_id=<id>. 3) Sometimes returns nothing; other times returns a trace missing 1-3 spans. Sample IDs (they provided these exact strings):
```
req-8f3a2b9c
req-8f3a2b9d
req-8f3a2b9e
req-9a1c4d22
```
They say this is intermittent (~1 in 5 requests) and started after the 2026-03-09 deploy.

Maya (eng-sre): tagging @eng-ml and infra — can you paste the query they're using in Console? Also any relevant errors in span ingestion pipeline?

Eli (eng-ml): Noticed something similar in the telemetry yesterday but assumed transient. Customer query pattern? Might be related to our join between request_id index and span_store TTL.

Jordan (support): Customer query: `/api/console/v1/traces?filter=request_id:REQ-ID-HERE&start=2026-03-10T13:50Z&end=2026-03-10T14:10Z` (they url-encoded req id). They also tried the UI trace panel search and saw blanks.

Alex (devex): Can you check whether the request_id -> trace mapping is using the right indexing pipeline? We recently added a prefix normalization step during ingest (strip `req-`?), maybe mismatch.

Maya (eng-sre): Quick checks I ran: 1) span_ingest logs show occasional 429s to the metadata-service around 14:02-14:06 UTC. 2) KV cache reports evictions on the mapping shard `trace-links-3` at ~14:03. 3) No obvious data corruption in blobstore.

Eli (eng-ml): If the metadata writes were throttled, we might have lost the write that links request_id -> trace_id while spans still landed in span_store. That would explain present spans without a linking row. Need to confirm write-ahead retries.

Jordan (support): Customer also attached a chunk of logs showing a 500 from `trace-linker` in front of one of the missing IDs. Snippet:```
2026-03-10T14:03:11Z ERROR trace-linker [req=req-8f3a2b9d] 500 internal: write timeout to meta-store
```

Maya (eng-sre): Filing a short-term workaround: increase retry window in linker and surface an active fallback for UI to search by span ID if request_id lookup fails. Can someone pick that up?

Eli (eng-ml): I'll investigate whether the linker commit is idempotent; if retries are safe we can bump retries. Also will check whether the prefix normalization change (Alex mentioned) could cause inconsistent keys when a retry arrives with different normalized form.

Alex (devex): Confirmed normalization was rolled on 2026-03-09 22:11 UTC (deploy 2026-03-09-22:00). It strips `req-` if present. If older linker instances used raw `req-8f3a...` and newer ones write `8f3a...`, mismatch is possible. We'll need a migration or dual-write compat layer.

Maya (eng-sre): Short plan: (1) Roll changer to dual-write normalized + raw for 1 hour; (2) Increase linker retries; (3) Backfill missing mappings for the window 2026-03-09T22:00 -> 2026-03-10T15:00 by scanning spans for request_id tag. I'll open infra tasks.

Jordan (support): I told the customer we're investigating and proposing a mitigation. They asked for an ETA for the rollback/dual-write.

Rae (customer-success): Customer prefers a patch rather than rollback. They asked for a 4-6 hour patch window.

Maya (eng-sre): Assigning tasks: Eli -> linker retry/idempotency + dual-write code; Alex -> confirm deploy plan and feature flag; I'll open a backfill job and monitor KV hotness. Targeting patch in next 3 hours.

infra-bot: Deploy pipeline queued for `trace-linker/dual-write` (PR #4921) — estimated run time 12m.

Eli (eng-ml): PR opened, tests passing. Will coordinate with Maya for canary.

Jordan (support): I'll update customer with target patch ETA ~3h and provide a SRE contact for on-call. Will post results here once the deploy and backfill complete. :thumbsup:

Maya (eng-sre): Please add any additional sample req IDs from the customer to the backfill ticket. Also flag if any high-priority customers are affected.

Rae (customer-success): Sending more IDs and a spreadsheet now.

Jordan (support): Thanks everyone — keeping this thread as the single source for the escalation.
